title: UPSTYLE_Backdoor_Investigation_2e9
description: Investigate a potential compromise involving the UPSTYLE backdoor malware on Linux systems.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The organization has detected unusual network activity on its internal systems. Your team has been tasked with investigating a potential compromise involving a backdoor malware named UPSTYLE. This malware is known to execute additional commands via specially crafted network requests and has been observed on Linux systems.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have access to the target system as user 'cyrano' with password 'cyrano'. The target system is connected to other systems in the network that may have been affected. Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content: You have access to the target system as user 'cyrano' with password 'cyrano'. The target system is connected to other systems in the network that may have been affected. Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content: While monitoring the target system, you noticed an unusual service running. Investigate the running services on the target system and identify any suspicious or unauthorized services.
levels.solution: Check the systemd services and look for any services that don't belong to standard system applications. The service name is stored in /tmp/flag1.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the systemd services and look for any services that don't belong to standard system applications.

levels.title: C2 Communication Discovery (Port)
levels.content: The suspicious service appears to be communicating with an external command-and-control (C2) server. Determine which network port is used for this suspicious communication.
levels.solution: Investigate the network connections made by the suspicious service. The C2 port number is stored in /tmp/flag2.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Investigate the network connections made by the suspicious service.

levels.title: Lateral Movement Investigation
levels.content: There is evidence that the attacker may have moved laterally from the target system to another system in the network. Investigate file transfers or remote execution used to move between hosts.
levels.solution: Check the system logs and network connections for any signs of lateral movement. The destination host is stored in /tmp/flag3.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the system logs and network connections for any signs of lateral movement.
